Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1b) shows a well-defined cystic lesion in the right lower lobe containing a distinct band-like opacity (indicated by arrows), which is characteristic of a dilated pulmonary vein traversing an intrapulmonary cyst. This specific anatomical relationship poses a risk of air embolism if the cyst is inadvertently punctured or ruptures, distinguishing it from simple benign cysts or other pathologies like sequestration or abscess which have different radiographic features.
